title: Per-tenant probation windows and decay-based circuit breaker
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Background: We need smarter automatic fallback triggers for region/tier routing that avoid noisy single-window thresholds. Current trip logic (global sliding window on 429/timeouts) causes large-scale fallbacks during bursty traffic and punishes healthy downstream tenants.

Problem: One-size-fits-all trip scores produce false positives for customers with short-lived spikes and don't support per-tenant SLAs. We lack a probation/probing mechanism to allow a route to recover without immediate global rollbacks.

Proposal: Implement a per-tenant, decay-based circuit-breaker with probation windows and multi-signal fusion. Key concepts: 1) Per-tenant trip score aggregated across metrics (429 rate, p50/p95 latency, timeout count, error-rate) with configurable weights; 2) Exponential decay on trip score to allow recovery over time (half-life tunable per tier); 3) Probation windows where a flagged tenant is routed to a degraded model variant at a low percentage (canary) while health probes run; 4) Escalation steps: soft-degrade (re-route to lower tier variant), probation canary (5-20%), hard-cut (100% fallback) with cooldowns; 5) Hysteresis: require sustained improvement before restoring full traffic; 6) Per-tenant thresholds and overrides for enterprise customers.

Design details: - Trip scoring: normalized signals -> weighted sum -> thresholding. Default weights: 0.4*error_rate + 0.3*timeout_rate + 0.2*p95_latency_penalty + 0.1*429_rate_adjusted. - Decay: continuous-time decay applied every second using configurable half-life (default 15 minutes for hosted, 5 minutes for dedicated). - Probation: when score exceeds soft threshold, move X% traffic to fallback variant for Y minutes while probing on production traffic and synthetic probes. - Escalation policy: if probation probe fails (probe fail rate > Z%), escalate to wider fallback. - Observability: emit trip_score, decay_constant, probation_state, last_probe_result, per-tenant history to Console and routing traces. - Overrides: enterprise customers can pin variants or opt out of automatic fallback. - Config surface: per-tenant/tier policy JSON with weights, thresholds, half_life, probation_pct, escalation_steps.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement scoring + decay in staging routing mesh behind a feature flag. 2) Add per-tenant policy store (read-mostly) with default policies. 3) Integrate small-traffic probation canaries and synthetic probe harness. 4) End-to-end test with chaos scenarios (429 floods, timeouts, noisy neighbor) and compare against current behavior. 5) Gradual rollout: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% for hosted; dedicated customers opt-in initially.

Why different from existing tickets: Prior tickets focused on global/federated circuit-breakers and threshold-driven fallbacks. This ticket prioritizes per-tenant recovery (probation windows), decay semantics, and an explicit canary/probe stage to reduce overreaction and improve customer fairness.

Metrics to watch: restoration false-positive rate, mean time to restore, overall fallback rate, per-tenant SLO violations, number of full-cut fallbacks per week.
acceptance_criteria: Routing mesh supports per-tenant trip_score aggregation and exposes trip_score metric to Console (per-tenant + route)
Decay implementation reduces trip_score over time and is configurable per policy (unit test coverage + integration verification)
Probation canary successfully routes configured percentage to fallback variant and synthetic probes run during probation window
Escalation steps trigger correctly based on probe results and sustained failures (end-to-end test assertions)
No customer experiences blind global fallback during staged rollout (compare to control group)
Documentation (Console + runbook) updated with how to interpret trip_score and how enterprise customers can opt out/override
